az_8b_boulder_the.blurb: Two large granite boulders on Mount Lemmon above Tucson, tucked into Gandalf's Gorge and reached by walking past a neighbouring boulder to the farther of the pair. All 14 problems are bouldering, and the spread is wide: a few easy lines around V1 to V4, then a steep jump into the hard stuff, with a cluster of V10 and V11 problems and a couple of V12 and V13 testpieces on top. Expect distinctive features, quality stone and a handful of projects still being worked. It suits strong boulderers more than beginners, though a few friendly warm-ups exist.

az_cave_wall.blurb: A mid-mountain sport wall on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalinas, one of three walls in the Outcroppings and reached by a short uphill walk from the road. The 14 bolted routes are mostly moderate: a few in the 5.5 to 5.8 range, five at 5.9 and five at 5.10. Lines are steep and pumpy, and many have a ledge partway up. The wall catches the morning sun and goes into shade by mid-afternoon, which makes it a comfortable choice on warm days. A cave at the south end gives cover from sun or rain. Good for climbers stepping up to 5.10.
az_cave_wall.parking_note: Drive the Mount Lemmon highway to about mile marker 19.4, just before the Ranger Station, and turn left onto Organization Ridge Road. After 0.3 miles you reach the Palisades Trailhead parking.
az_cave_wall.approach: From the parking, walk a short way along the road, then take the path on the left and follow cairns uphill to the top of the Cave and Tall walls, roughly 15 to 20 minutes. A path leads down from there to the wall.

az_fun_ship.blurb: A small south-facing crag shaped a bit like a ship, one of the subareas near Chimney Rock in West Sedona. It has 14 routes of mixed style: eight sport, four top-rope and two trad, mostly from 5.7 to 5.10. Many lines climb through a limestone band, where small to medium cams help on the trad lines, and then finish on the cleaner rock above. The approach is a pleasant walk across flat red sandstone, so it works well as a short outing for newer leaders and groups who want some easier climbs.

az_helmet_the.blurb: A small sport crag on Mount Lemmon in the Windy Ridge section, easy to spot from the highway because the formation looks like a helmet sitting on the slope. The face is vertical on the left and there is a shallow cave on the right with roof climbs. All 14 routes are bolted, starting around 5.9 and stacking up heavily in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with two at 5.13. Faces west and gets shade in the morning. The short walk in makes it a handy stop for strong sport climbers.

az_planet_earth_wall.blurb: A long, steep sport wall on the shady south side of the Virgin River Gorge, beside Mentor Cave in the Arizona Strip. Expect overhanging terrain with a low roof band and a hard, sustained feel: of the 14 routes, nearly all fall between 5.12 and 5.14, with seven at 5.13 and a couple of 5.14 lines. The approach is a roughly 10 minute walk from the parking, passing beneath the freeway. Traffic noise is constant, and the gorge is best in the cooler months, from October to April.

az_sphinx.blurb: A small crag high on Mount Lemmon, reached from the Bear Canyon side of the Santa Catalinas. It holds 14 routes, a mix of trad (eight) and sport (six), with grades from 5.9 up to 5.12 and the bulk of them around 5.11. The stone is sharp, and some newer lines are a little grainy but should clean up with traffic. Thick manzanita has kept visitor numbers low. The east face warms on sunny winter days while the west side warms later, so you can chase the sun or shade. Best for climbers comfortable at 5.10 and above.

az_stonewall_aka_airmen_peak.blurb: A traditional-only crag in the lower foothills of Mount Lemmon near Tucson, with climbing on its south, east and north faces. All 14 routes need gear, from 5.6 to 5.10, with the middle grades most common; doubled cams up to a number 4 are useful, and the longer east and north face lines call for two ropes. Rock is mostly better than its reputation suggests. It sees few visitors and is not heavily manicured. The walk in is long and runs up a canyon, so allow a big day. Fall through spring is the time to go.

az_sterling_pass.blurb: A sandstone cliff band beside the Sterling Pass trail in Oak Creek Canyon, north of Sedona. It is a crack-focused crag: of 14 routes, twelve are trad and two are sport, with most between 5.10 and 5.12 and a single route near 5.8. Several are multi-pitch lines of five or six pitches. Reaching the base takes a steady uphill hike of more than a mile that gains over a thousand feet, so it is not a quick stop. Suited to experienced climbers with a full rack who want long crack climbing away from the busier canyon crags.
